summary: Adds tenant-aware Sign in with Apple support with form-post callbacks and dynamically signed, broker-backed Apple client secrets.
userImpact: Users can sign in to an enabled EnterpriseGlue tenant with their Apple ID.
Administrators can configure Apple Team ID, Key ID, Services ID, and a broker-managed private-key reference on an OIDC provider.
configuration: Apple OIDC providers set clientAuthentication to apple_private_key_jwt, clientId to the Apple Services ID, appleTeamId and appleKeyId to the Developer account values, and applePrivateKeyRef to a tenant-secret-backed .p8 key reference.
Register the exact HTTPS tenant callback URL with the Apple Services ID and keep the provider disabled until its private key is available through the tenant secret broker.

changes: OIDC provider configuration accepts Apple client-authentication metadata and a private-key secret reference.
The global and tenant-qualified OIDC callback routes also accept bounded application/x-www-form-urlencoded POST responses.

security: Apple client secrets are generated just in time as short-lived ES256 JWTs; the Apple .p8 private key remains behind the tenant secret broker and is never persisted in provider configuration.
Apple POST callbacks retain signed-state, browser-cookie, nonce, tenant-routing, reconciliation, and session-issuance checks; generic OIDC providers continue to use PKCE.
Apple first-authorization profile names are accepted only after the callback email matches the signed ID-token email and after bounded character validation; they never affect authorization.
POST callback bodies are content-type checked and size bounded before provider state is consumed.
documentation: Operator configuration and Apple Developer registration guidance in docs/how-to/auth-sso.md
knownLimitations: Apple Developer Services ID, domain, return URL, and signing-key registration must be completed in the customer's Apple Developer account before the provider can be enabled.
rollback: Disable the Apple identity provider, revoke its active EnterpriseGlue sessions, and retire the broker-managed Apple private key before rolling back the application images.
validation: OIDC service tests for Apple authorization parameters, ES256 client-secret claims and headers, broker-backed key resolution, and token exchange.
Backend route tests for tenant-qualified and compatibility POST callbacks, callback rejection, state binding, and payload limits.
Schema, API, frontend, typecheck, and release-note preflight checks.
